claims.text: Embedding controlled SRO precipitates in crystalline silicon will enhance phonon scattering.
Enhanced phonon scattering from SRO precipitates will reduce the lattice thermal conductivity of silicon.
High-quality crystalline silicon is a nonmetallic host with negligible electronic thermal conduction.
Well-controlled nanoscale SRO precipitates can be introduced into a silicon matrix.
Phonon conduction dominates silicon heat transport from room temperature to moderately high temperatures under conditions with minimal electronic contributions.
Localized SRO precipitates disrupt long-range crystal order in silicon.
Localized SRO precipitates act as phonon-scattering centers.
Additional scattering sites created by SRO precipitates reduce phonon scattering times.
Reduced phonon scattering times lower the efficiency of lattice energy transport.
Silicon containing SRO precipitates will have measurably lower lattice thermal conductivity than pristine single-crystal silicon.
The magnitude of the thermal-conductivity reduction depends on precipitate density, size, and spatial distribution.
The precipitate-induced effect should be observable primarily when phonon-mediated heat conduction is dominant.
A statistically significant decrease in thermal conductivity or a change in phonon scattering time can be tested by comparing precipitate-bearing silicon against pristine silicon.
